messages:
jamie-cs: FYI customer on dedicated reported intermittent 429s this morning even though they have a reserved pool sized for their QPS. They see spikes ~1.2k rps for a couple minutes and then 429s. Customer says SLA says <100ms p50 and 99.9% availability — they're worried.

sarah-sre: Can you paste a sample request/response headers (no PII)? most likely mismatch between reserved pool rate cap and token-level rate-limiter or short burst window.

jamie-cs: Pasting sanitized curl + headers they captured: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer redacted" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Limit: 500
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset: 24
X-Redwood-Reserved-Pool: pool-1234
X-Redwood-Reserved-Pool-Capacity: 600
X-Redwood-Reserved-Pool-Used: 596
Retry-After: 2
```
They said their app bursts up to ~1.2k for <60s and then backs off; pool capacity supposedly 600 - not sure how that maps to their committed throughput.

ingrid-eng: Two quick notes: (1) "Reserved-Pool-Capacity" is expressed as concurrent request slots / throughput units depending on pool config (they can be tok/sec-limited or concurrent). (2) Rate limiter enforces a short moving-window burst allowance (default 60s) + a long-term average to protect multi-tenant hosts. If they hit the short burst repeatedly across many keys, we clamp them.

jamie-cs: @ingrid-eng any quick checks I can ask the customer to run? they want repro steps we can monitor.

ingrid-eng: Ask them to hit a single endpoint at controlled rate with this script to reproduce. 
```
# reproduce.sh
for i in {1..180}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"hi"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs &
  sleep 0.1
done
```
They should run with a single key and capture response headers. If they get sustained 429s while X-Redwood-Reserved-Pool-Used < Capacity, then it's a routing/fallback problem.

sarah-sre: I pulled the pool config for pool-1234: autoscale=false, burst_window=60s, cap_type=throughput, throughput_cap=600u/s, headroom_policy=0.1 (10% internal headroom). That means effective cap visible to customer ~540u/s. If they're counting different units (requests vs tokens) could mismatch.

jamie-cs: So that explains some of the gap but they're still seeing 429s when used ~596 which is >540 effective. But their captures show X-Redwood-Reserved-Pool-Used 596 and cap 600 — they'd expect to still get some headroom.

ingrid-eng: Two possibilities: (A) tokenization causing high tokens per request so our throughput units are consumed faster, (B) rate-limiter global smoothing kicked in because the operator cluster observed a past burst from other pools and applied a quick protective throttle. Check cloud-metrics: "pool-1234.throughput.1m" and host-level "node.*.egress_rate".

jamie-cs: I asked for their average tokens per request over the spike window — customer returned ~1.8k tokens/request due to long context. That would blow up throughput units.

sarah-sre: ok that aligns. We should communicate two remediation steps: 1) Convert their pool from simple throughput cap to token-aware throughput (quantify units) OR 2) add short-term burst allowance for their account by raising headroom_policy to 0.25 for 15m window while they smooth client-side. I can patch config if you want.

alex-sales: Customer is on an enterprise contract, they want quick mitigation + note to avoid billing surprises. If we change headroom, can we guarantee no noisy-neighbor risk?

sarah-sre: We can temporarily raise headroom to 25% for that pool and set a 15m guard timer. We'll monitor node egress and global throttles. Noisy-neighbor risk low since it's dedicated pool but host-level protection still exists — we'll keep an eye.

ops-bot: Deploy queued: apply-pool-headroom-adjust for pool-1234 by sarah-sre. CI tests: rate-limiter smoke.

ops-bot: Deploy success: headroom updated to 25% for pool-1234 (rollout id r-20250412-07).

jamie-cs: Patched and informed customer to retry and to run reproduce.sh. Customer reported after 8 minutes: "errors dropped to near zero, p50 latency ~110ms, occasional 429s during 2s windows then normalizing."

ingrid-eng: Follow-up: we should add a note to run token-trim or reduce context for high-QPS bursts. Also adding a tooltip in Console explaining "throughput units vs tokens" would help.

jamie-cs: Customer happy for now but asked for a root-cause writeup for their ops team. I'll prepare a short blurb: explanation of token units, effective capacity = throughput_cap*(1-headroom_policy), and recommended client-side smoothing + token budget per request.

alex-sales: Please cc me on the blurb. They may convert more traffic to Dedicated if this pattern stabilizes.

sarah-sre: I'll draft the blurb and include exact metrics we saw. Also creating an alert in Console: reserved-pool-used > 0.9 * capacity for > 30s.

jamie-cs: Closing the thread once blurb + alert are live. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sarah-sre: Filed follow-up ticket ENG-9123 to add Console tooltip + telemetry dashboard for tokens vs throughput.

jamie-cs: (tag) resolved for now. Will re-open if it recurs. :white_check_mark:
